newsitem.title: USA: Stocks fall on earnings, rate jitters.
newsitem.headline: Stocks fall on earnings, rate jitters.

text.p: Stocks fell Thursday as investors worried about corporate earnings and rising long-term interest rates ahead of a meeting of Federal Reserve policy-makers next week.
The dollar ended mixed and oil prices fell. Gold edged higher.

The Dow Jones industrial average lost 35.73 points to close at 7,654.25. In the broader market, declining issues led advances 1,455 to 1,300 on heavy volume of 499 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.

It was the fourth day this week that stocks were subject to sharp swings. On Monday, the Dow had its second-biggest point loss ever, 192 points, and on Tuesday it rose 154 points, and fell 68 points Wednesday when it swung widely in the plus and minus columns.
Since the start of May, the blue-chip Dow index has risen nearly 700 points, or 9.7 percent, fostering doubts about whether the run-up will continue.
"People are nervous as cats out there and they are doing some selling to nail down profits," said Marshall Acuff, chief investment strategest for Smith Barney.
Analysts said stocks were jarred by the steady rise in long-term rates, which have risen for four straight days.
The 30-year Treasury fell 17/32, raising its yield to 6.78 percent from 6.74 percent on Wednesday. The price and yield move in opposite directions.

"Yields have backed up here above 6.77 percent. A combination of that, plus portfolio juggling, and many feel we've had a monstrous run and stocks need to consolidate," said Scott Bleier, chief investment strategist at Prime Charter Ltd.
Another warning of lower profits, from technology company Komag Inc., also cooled thirst for stocks, analysts said.

"For the past three quarters, there has been a sense of hesitancy and nervousness before earnings get reported. We are heading into the reporting period, and this quarter shouldn't be any different," Acuff said.

Wall Street was also on edge -- as is traditional -- ahead of the meeting next Tuesday and Wednesday of Fed policy-makers though most economists expect the central bank to hold short-term interest rates steady for now.

In currency markets, the dollar fell to Canadian $1.3817 from C$1.3937 late on Wednesday after the Bank of Canada surprised investors by raising official interest rates. It also slid to 113.10 Japanese yen from 113.92. But the dollar edged up to 1.7260 German marks from 1.7240 late on Wednesday.
Oil fell as traders grew sceptical that the Organisation of Petroleum Exporting Countries would be able to rein in overproduction following pledges by members to do so.
Crude oil for August delivery fell 43 cents to $19.09 a barrel at the New York Mercantile Exchange.
August gold added 80 cents to $339.80 an ounce at New York's Commodity Exchange.
Overseas, London's FTSE 100 rose 17.9 points to 4,657.9. Tokyo's 225-share Nikkei average closed at 20,624.76, down 54.51 points.
